notes.399.2: Line 399.2 is Latin and comes from a different tablet; 'quis' and 'vae' are hard to construe, and 'who [it is]' is a guess. Lines 46146.1 to 4 are in Gaulish, not Latin, and most of lines 1 to 3 is of disputed meaning, so the rendering is tentative throughout. The senses assumed are uediiumi 'I invoke', diiiuion 'of the gods', andedion and anderon 'of the nether ones', brixtia 'magic', sos 'them', adgarion 'accuser'; risun, artiu, lopites and sniEddic are obscure. Mapon(os) Arueriiatis is a god, with an epithet perhaps meaning 'of the Arverni'. The names in line 4 are Latin names in Gaulish accusative form; Aemili- runs on into the next line.

nodes.text: [R]ead, go, look for who [it is]: woe [to you], [to you].
Of the nether (?) gods (?) I invoke (?), by means of (?)
torment (?) and bind (?) them by the magic of the nether ones (?):
Gaius Lucius Florus Nigrinus the accuser (?), Aemili-
